claims.kickoff_quote:
*(only if the retro surfaced a workflow this project keeps repeating by hand)*
Use the writing-skills skill to codify that repeated workflow into a real dev-kit skill, so the next milestone inherits it instead of re-deriving it. Only do this for a pattern that actually recurred and is reusable beyond this milestone — a one-off sequence is not a skill.
claims.reasoning: KICKOFF sets the creation bar at 'a workflow THIS PROJECT keeps repeating' that is 'reusable beyond this MILESTONE', and sends the result into dev-kit (the cross-project kit). The skill sets a strictly higher bar — 'You'd reference this again across projects' (line 51), 'Pattern applies broadly (not project-specific)' (line 52) — and explicitly excludes 'Project-specific conventions (put in your instructions file)' (line 58). An agent following KICKOFF will commit a project-scoped workflow into dev-kit-core that the skill would have told it to put in the instructions file instead. The two gates disagree about what qualifies, so this is a contradiction rather than mere redundancy.

You'd reference this again across projects' (line 51). The 'actually recurred' half is separately enforced by the skill's provenance guard — 'If you cannot find one, refuse and ask for a successful run first' (line 74). The KICKOFF sentence re-derives a gate the skill already enforces in two places. (Note: this same sentence is also the source of the contradiction in writing-skills-1 — the restatement is not just redundant, it restates the rule with a weakened threshold.)
